message.content:
Yes—if you’re experiencing excessive or disruptive noise in Atlanta, you can file a complaint with the city’s authorities. Here’s how it works: | Step | What to Do | Where to File | Contact Info | |------|------------|---------------|--------------| | **1** | Identify the source & time of the noise | • City of Atlanta Police Department (for immediate disturbances)
• City of Atlanta Department of Public Safety (for ongoing or repeated violations) | • 311 (non-emergency)
• 404‑656‑3111 (Atlanta Police) | | **2** | Gather details | • Date & time of incidents
• Exact location (address or intersection)
• Description of the noise (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs)
• Any evidence (photos, videos, audio recordings) | • Online form at https://www.atlantaga.gov/311
• Email: noisecomplaints@atlantaga.gov | | **3** | Submit the complaint | • Online via the 311 portal
• Phone call to 311 or 404‑656‑3111
• Mail or fax to the Department of Public Safety | • Mailing address: 1000 Peachtree Street NW, Atlanta, GA 30303
• Fax: 404‑656‑3111 | | **4** | Follow up | • You’ll receive a reference number.
• If the issue persists, you can contact your local city council member’s office for additional support. | • Find your council member: https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/city-council | ### Quick Tips * **Immediate emergencies** (e.g., a neighbor’s party that’s causing a disturbance after hours) – call 911 if you feel unsafe or if the noise is accompanied by other illegal activity. * **Non-emergencies** – use 311 or the online portal; this is the fastest way to get a response from the city’s noise enforcement team. * **Persistent problems** – keep a log of dates/times and any responses you receive. This documentation helps when you bring the issue to your council member’s office. If you’re unsure which department to contact, start with the 311 system—it will route your complaint to the appropriate agency. Good luck!
